agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability for CMS content. The central attachment point is useContent (src/hooks/useContent.ts), which is the single hook through which 236+ consumers retrieve Contentstack content via getContentByKey(). Integrating Live Preview there propagates updates to all downstream components without touching them individually. Contentstack external services are unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to the boundary with mocked assumptions.

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a useful architectural note about useContent being the central integration point for 236+ consumers. I built the full AC list from scratch based on the story title ('Live Preview of Content in CMS'), the three-site scope (GO, UP, MX), and the identified files. Key design decisions: (1) AC-1 sets a 5-second SLA for preview updates based on typical WebSocket latency expectations — this may need adjustment based on actual Contentstack Live Preview SDK behavior. (2) AC-7 ensures preview infrastructure is completely absent in production builds — critical security requirement. (3) AC-8 addresses rapid-edit debouncing to prevent render storms. (4) AC-11 ensures cross-site isolation since all three sites share the same codebase but have separate Contentstack stacks. (5) AC-9 and AC-13 address resource cleanup. CAVEAT: I did not have access to the actual file contents of useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, or ContentstackLink.tsx. If Live Preview is already partially implemented, or if the architecture differs from openspec's description (e.g., useContent does not exclusively use getContentByKey, or ContentstackLink has its own data fetching), some ACs may need adjustment. I recommend reviewing these ACs against the actual source before implementation.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Openspec provided architectural context (useContent as central hook for 236+ consumers, test-time boundary mocking) but left acceptance criteria empty — it did not elaborate requirements or propose ACs as expected. Speckit then compensated by building 13 ACs from scratch, covering SLA, security, debouncing, cross-site isolation, and cleanup. The agents added non-overlapping value (architecture scoping vs. AC authoring), but the pipeline inverted: speckit performed openspec's core job. Critically, speckit explicitly flagged it had no access to actual source files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) and recommends human review against real source before implementation. ACs authored without source inspection are unverifiable for correctness.
